title: Regular sleepers had 38% lower depression risk than irregular ones in UK Biobank, even when the irregular group slept 7+ hours. Are you tracking regularity?
text:
This one changed how I look at my own sleep data. In a UK Biobank analysis of about 80,000 people with wrist accelerometers, regular sleepers had a 38% lower risk of later depression and a 33% lower risk of anxiety than irregular sleepers. The part that stuck with me is that irregular sleepers who still hit the recommended hours kept the higher risk.

It's observational, so it can't say irregular sleep causes anything. But most of us optimise for hours and deep sleep percentage, and very few apps even show a regularity score.

For anyone who has tried fixing their bed and wake times within a 30 minute window for a few weeks: did anything change in how you felt, or in your HRV and resting heart rate? And which wearable or app shows regularity well?

(Disclosure: I run a small supplement company, so weigh my take accordingly. No products or links in this post.)
